subject.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full

question: Should `security="full"` bypass the ambiguous-interpreter script-preflight rejection for approval-gated `ask="on-miss"` and `ask="always"`, or only for YOLO `ask="off"`?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but it changes when OpenClaw skips a fail-closed exec preflight gate, so the permanent trust boundary needs maintainer intent rather than reviewer inference.

options.title: Accept full-security bypass after docs fix
options.body: Treat `security="full"` as the trust gate regardless of ask mode, but first restore the docs caveat that YOLO skips all script preflight.

options.title: Keep YOLO-only bypass
options.body: Revise code, tests, and docs so only `security="full"` plus `ask="off"` bypasses ambiguous-interpreter rejection.

options.title: Defer under the linked security issue
options.body: Pause this PR until the protected linked issue gets an explicit security-policy decision.

recommendation.title: Accept full-security bypass after docs fix
recommendation.body: Treat `security="full"` as the trust gate regardless of ask mode, but first restore the docs caveat that YOLO skips all script preflight.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on exec approval policy and docs for the affected trust-boundary surface.
